author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire Public Radio says local law enforcement played a significant role in the state’s increase in immigration arrests this summer, based on federal data obtained through public-records requests by the Deportation Data Project.

The analysis found that local police departments accounted for nearly half of the 198 people detained in New Hampshire from May through July. More than 700 people have been detained in the state since the start of the second Trump administration, NHPR reported.

The departments involved use agreements known as 287(g) programs, which allow local officers to carry out certain immigration actions while working with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. New Hampshire is the only New England state where local law-enforcement agencies have signed such agreements, according to NHPR.

Since September 2025, local agencies had arrested 172 people through a 287(g) program, with arrests concentrated in the southern half of the state and around the ICE office in Manchester. Hillsborough and Rockingham counties also have sheriff’s-office agreements.

NHPR’s review said arrests involved people from 48 countries and that about one-third of those arrested during the Trump administration had a criminal conviction. The data is likely to remain part of a wider debate over the role of local police in federal immigration enforcement.
dek: A data review says local departments accounted for nearly half of 198 people detained in New Hampshire from May through July as 287(g) partnerships expanded.
headline: NH police departments tied to surge in ICE arrests, NHPR analysis finds
